cards.title: Document Intelligence on One GPU: what it is
questions: what is the document intelligence on one gpu case study
what is the document intelligence evaluation
explain the document intelligence evaluation project
what is the local model document reading evaluation
what did the document intelligence evaluation measure
which local model reads what
summary of the document intelligence case study
tell me about the document intelligence evaluation for ocr tables charts
what is the eleven models by seven tasks evaluation
what is the 40,975 scored rows evaluation
why did she build the document intelligence evaluation
what is the october 2026 model evaluation case study
cards.answer: It's a model evaluation case study from October 2026 called Document Intelligence on One GPU: Which Local Model Reads What. I measured eleven open-weight models across seven tasks (prose OCR, tables, chart questions, chart to table, whole-page text, layout and contract clauses) under a frozen protocol, then confirmed the winners on data no model had seen. The result is 40,975 scored rows for rounds 1 and 2, with no scores given by a model judge. The deployment target is a single NVIDIA L4 or L40S, and I used public benchmarks only.

cards.title: The problem: facts hidden in hard-to-read places
questions: what problem does the document intelligence evaluation solve
why is document extraction hard in the document intelligence evaluation
what counts as solved in the document intelligence evaluation
what kinds of extraction does a proposal packet need
why can't a search box read these document packets
why not use a cloud document service for these documents
why does the document intelligence study say a single accuracy number hides the problem
what does fluent text that is 90% right mean in the evaluation
what are the five kinds of extraction in one packet
which documents was the document intelligence evaluation built for
problem statement for the one gpu document study
what has to be true for an extracted record to be useful
cards.answer: The most useful facts in proposals, contracts, awards and reports sit in scanned text, budget tables, charts, spreadsheets flattened into PDF and clauses on page forty. A database can't read them and neither can a search box. Each kind of extraction fails differently, so one accuracy number hides the one that matters. I defined solved as three things: the numbers are right, the source page is attached, and the system says so when it is unsure or couldn't read a page. Fluent text that is 90% right is a liability in a budget. Many of these documents also can't leave the organization.

cards.answer: Every score comes from a published answer key and code, never from another model's opinion, so there are zero model-judge scores. Failed and truncated answers stay in the denominator as zero, and nothing is re-run to rescue them. Only one model sits on the GPU at a time, the deployment target is an L4 with 24 GB or an L40S with 48 GB, and every model was measured on one 32 GB desktop so speeds compare fairly. I used public datasets only, so every number can be published and checked.

cards.answer: Eleven open-weight models. The Qwen family covers Qwen3-VL 8B Instruct and Qwen2.5-VL 7B on Ollama, Qwen3-VL 32B AWQ and Qwen3 32B text on vLLM, and Qwen2.5-VL 32B on Ollama. A locally tagged 27B build is reported but not recommended, because I couldn't verify its upstream identity. The final round added three small parsers on vLLM, Nemotron 3.5 Parse 0.63B, PaddleOCR-VL-1.6 and olmOCR-2 7B FP8, plus gpt-oss-20b for clauses. Nemotron 3 Nano 30B ran through a hosted API on the legal track.

cards.title: The seven tasks and their datasets
questions: what tasks were in the document intelligence evaluation

cards.answer: Each kind of hard-to-reach information became one frozen task with its own public answer key and metric. Prose crop OCR used 50 OmniDocBench cases scored by character error rate and numeric recall. Table transcription used OmniDocBench and FinTabNet.c with 60 cases, scored by TEDS tree similarity and cell F1. Chart questions used 200 ChartQA cases with relaxed accuracy at 5% tolerance. Chart to table used 60 cases, whole-page text 40 scored by word F1, layout detection 120 at IoU 0.5, and clause extraction 24 cases from CUAD and ContractNLI, with 60 fresh documents on top. Tables, chart questions and pages also had held-out or fresh sets.

cards.title: Prompting methods compared
questions: what methods were compared in the document intelligence evaluation
what is self-check in the document intelligence evaluation

what is the baseline prompt in the evaluation

cards.answer: Besides the baseline (task prompt, forced JSON schema, temperature 0), I tried an expert prompt with a role and rules, and self-check, where the model answers and then re-reads the image and corrects itself in one call. Upscale or hires enlarges the image first. Round 2 added vote3 (three answers, majority wins), read table first (transcribe the chart data, then answer) and layout masking (blank detected figures and tables before page OCR). The legal track used evidence by ID, and the final round compared each parser's official multipass or pipeline mode with its single pass.

cards.title: Making numbers comparable across two machines
questions: how did the document intelligence evaluation keep results comparable

what token budgets and image caps were used for every model
how are held-out sets used once in the document intelligence study

cards.answer: The desktop and laptop ran weeks apart under different runtimes, so I checked sameness in code. A conformance check fingerprints the frozen case manifests, the exact requests, the model-call settings and the scorers, and the merge tool refuses rows that fail. Cases were hashed before any model saw them, and held-out sets (2,181 cases in round 1, 1,988 in round 2) were used once. Every model got the same prompt, schema, token budget (300 to 6,000 by task) and image cap, at temperature 0. A thinking build burned its budget on hidden reasoning, so I removed it and deleted its rows. Qwen2.5-VL 7B reproduced in 11 of 13 comparison groups.

cards.answer: The final round tested four models never run before: three small parsers and gpt-oss-20b. I wrote the two leads down as hypotheses, then tested them on 100 FinTabNet.c tables and 80 unused OmniDocBench pages, all at an 8,192-token output budget against Qwen3-VL 32B AWQ. A hypothesis passed only if its main metric improved and numeric recall was no more than 0.02 worse, under a source-clustered bootstrap with Holm correction. PaddleOCR-VL-1.6 passed. Nemotron Parse stayed a lead. The parsers' multipass modes did not beat single pass, and a bigger budget recovered at most one failed page in 80.

cards.answer: PaddleOCR-VL-1.6 passed the pre-registered test on 100 fresh FinTabNet.c tables. Its TEDS was 0.852 against 0.762 for Qwen3-VL 32B AWQ, and numeric recall was 97.4% against 93.2%. It needs only about 2 GB of weights and was the leading table route. It still did not reach the 99% bar I set for unattended numbers, so it stays review-assisted. I read the pass narrowly: the model wins on this public data, and an organization's own tables still need their own labelled test.

cards.answer: Nemotron 3.5 Parse wrote better page text, with word F1 of 0.899 against 0.820 for Qwen3-VL 32B AWQ on 80 fresh pages. On numbers it tied on average, 88.2% against 88.3%, but 80 pages can't rule out a 0.02 deficit, so I count it as a lead with numbers still open, not a win. That's why the routing for whole pages says single pass with numbers checked. olmOCR-2 wrote the cleanest prose and lost the most numbers, at 70.6% numeric recall on those pages. The Nemotron parser is about 1.3 GB.

cards.title: Does a small 8B model read prose and tables as well as a 32B

cards.answer: On text tasks, size made little difference. Qwen3-VL 8B on the 12 GB laptop had a pooled character error of 1.2% on 50 prose crops on both machines, matching Qwen3-VL 32B AWQ and Qwen2.5-VL 32B. Table TEDS was 0.818 for 8B, 0.821 for the 32B AWQ build and 0.724 for 7B, and no prompt variant changed that significantly. But every model recovered 96.5% of the numbers in the crops, short of my 99% bar. For budgets and invoices the missing 3.5% is the whole problem, so the 8B model is a review-assisted candidate, not an unattended one.

cards.title: The self-check swing: +26.5 for 7B, minus 43.5 for 8B
questions: what happened when self-check was applied to chart questions

cards.answer: The same self-check instruction, on the same prompt and images, moved the two small models in opposite directions on 200 chart questions. Qwen2.5-VL 7B went from 52.5% to 79.0%, up 26.5 points. Qwen3-VL 8B went from 79.5% to 36.0%, down 43.5. The 32B reference scored 85.0% at baseline and 91.0% with self-check. The pattern held on fresh charts in round 2: plus 17.8 for 7B and minus 42.7 for 8B. A method isn't a global switch; it has to be chosen per model and per task, and confirmed on data the pairing hasn't seen.

cards.answer: Recovering the table behind a chart is where the 8B model needs help. On 60 charts, scored by value recall within 5% and label recall, self-check lifted Qwen3-VL 8B from 0.418 to 0.930, and the expert prompt reached 0.900. So self-check is the routed method for chart to data on 8B, even though it's harmful for chart questions on the same model. It's a 60-case task, a strong candidate that still needs a larger held-out set before I'd trust it.

cards.title: Round 2: vote3 and the fresh charts

cards.answer: Round 2 froze 1,322 new questions across 722 charts and 80 new pages, and I picked vote3 in advance as the one confirmatory method. It held up: plus 4.5 points on 7B (95% interval 3.0 to 6.1) and plus 2.6 on the desktop 32B (1.4 to 3.7). On 8B it did nothing, minus 0.2 with an interval crossing zero. Read-table-first was dropped on development data, and upscaling alone didn't help. Costs differ: self-check is one longer call and vote3 is three calls. For 7B, self-check is the cheap win. For 8B neither applies, and for 32B vote3 is the only confirmed gain.

cards.title: Layout masking: cleaner text, lost numbers
questions: what is the layout masking trade-off

cards.answer: Masking raised the word F1 and cut numeric recall, so I kept it experimental. A layout detector blanked figures and tables before page OCR. On the 80 confirmation pages, Qwen3-VL 32B AWQ word F1 rose from 0.814 to 0.881, while numeric recall fell from 0.872 to 0.694. On the 40 development pages it fell from 0.909 to 0.720, and newspaper results got worse. Masking also hid numbers the page text needed. For contracts and budgets that trade is unacceptable. Next I'll blank only tables, figures and equations and judge it on numeric recall first. 7B gained 0.085 on word F1, and 8B's 0.010 gain included zero.

cards.title: Evidence by ID: stopping invented quotes
questions: what is evidence by id in the document intelligence evaluation
how does the evidence-linked extraction work
why did models quote text that did not exist

does evidence by id prove the answer is right

how does retrieval coverage limit clause extraction

cards.answer: Early legal runs showed models quoting text that wasn't in the cited span, or paraphrasing it enough to fail a string check. The fix takes copying out of the model's hands. Documents are split into blocks with IDs, retrieval supplies candidates, and the model returns only IDs and the label. My code copies the exact text, verifies its hash and location, and records absent fields explicitly. That removed every copy failure from the quoting design, 0 failed requests against 2 to 4 for the baseline. It doesn't prove the answer is right, and retrieval is the bottleneck: if the right block isn't a candidate, no design recovers it.

cards.title: Nemotron reassessment: a bad score is a configuration
questions: why did nemotron 3 nano score low at first
what was the nemotron reassessment
how many requests were in the controlled nemotron reassessment
did enabling reasoning help nemotron on cuad

what was the cost of turning reasoning on in nemotron
how did she test one mechanism at a time

cards.answer: A hosted Nemotron 3 Nano 30B scored 1/12 on CUAD, far below the local Qwen models. The easy conclusion was weak model. The honest one was weak configuration, untested. I ran 192 requests across eight configurations on the same 24 cases, changing one mechanism at a time: budget, reasoning, sampling, label definitions, full-document context, evidence by ID and schema delivery. Budget alone changed nothing, and reasoning lifted CUAD from 1/12 to 4/12. A pre-specified contrast on 60 fresh documents confirmed it: CUAD 3/30 to 13/30, ContractNLI 5/30 to 12/30, at the cost of one truncation per task. That supports enabling reasoning. It doesn't show production adequacy or a serving defect.

cards.answer: On 60 fresh public documents with identical requests and a 16,000-token budget, Qwen3 32B with thinking off scored 14/30 on CUAD and 18/30 on ContractNLI; thinking on gave 15 and 16. gpt-oss-20b at low reasoning scored 15 and 14, and at high reasoning 11 and 4, because it got truncated. Nemotron with reasoning on scored 13 and 12. The CUAD set holds 15 absent fields, so answering absent every time scores 15/30, and no configuration beat that. At 30 questions a task, differences of a few documents are noise, so I don't claim a winner on CUAD.

cards.title: Hardware fit and speed on L4 and L40S
questions: what gpu does the document intelligence evaluation target

cards.answer: The target is one NVIDIA L4 (24 GB) or L40S (48 GB), but every final-round model ran on one 32 GB RTX 5090. Fit comes from weight sizes: about 2 GB for PaddleOCR-VL-1.6, 1.3 GB for Nemotron 3.5 Parse, 13 GB for gpt-oss-20b and 20 GB for a 4-bit 32B model. Everything recommended fits an L40S; on an L4 a 32B is tight. On a packet of 20 pages and 20 tables, four requests at a time, Nemotron Parse did 140 cases a minute, PaddleOCR-VL-1.6 73, olmOCR-2 19 and Qwen3-VL 32B AWQ 9. Bandwidth is about 1.8, 0.86 and 0.3 TB/s for the desktop, L40S and L4, so speeds there will be lower.

cards.title: What the evaluation does not show
questions: what are the limits of the document intelligence evaluation

cards.answer: It's prototype evidence, not production certification. I did not measure speed on an actual L4 or L40S, purchase cost, or any total cost against a hosted service. The ranking should transfer to the target cards; the absolute numbers won't. No model reached the 99% bar for unattended numeric extraction, and the best table route reached 97.4%. Public scores say which model to try first, but an organization's own documents need their own labelled, document-disjoint test. Fresh means unused in earlier runs, not proven absent from pretraining. A local pipeline is an architectural option, not a security certification, and I used NIST AI 600-1 as the risk framing.

cards.answer: Routing came straight from the measured results. Tables go to PaddleOCR-VL-1.6 single pass. Whole pages go to Nemotron 3.5 Parse single pass with numbers checked. Prose crops use Qwen3-VL 8B baseline. Chart questions use 8B with self-check off, or 7B with it on; chart to data uses 8B with self-check. Layout uses DocLayout-YOLO. Clauses use Qwen3 32B with thinking off, or gpt-oss-20b at low reasoning, with evidence by ID and retrieval coverage shown. Not ready: unattended numbers and masking where numbers matter. Native spreadsheets should be parsed directly; a spreadsheet printed to PDF needs the table route and a numeric check.

cards.title: My role and who did what
questions: what was her role in the document intelligence evaluation

cards.answer: My role was evaluation design, orchestration and failure analysis. Local models did all the reading, extraction and answering. AI coding assistants wrote and ran the harness, and no assistant read a page, a crop or a model answer. People read aggregate tables only. I set the protocol: frozen cases, identical requests, answer-key scoring, failures kept in the denominator and written-down hypotheses before confirmation. I also did the failure analysis, such as the self-check split between 7B and 8B and the numeric loss under masking.

cards.title: What comes next for the document intelligence work
questions: what are the next steps for the document intelligence evaluation
what is the intake pipeline plan
what is field-bound numbers scoring

what does the roadmap of the document intelligence case study include
cards.answer: Six steps, each with a done-when. First, an intake service on the routing: a queue, checkpoints, bounded retries and one model per task, done when every file in a packet is processed and resumable with page-level evidence. Second, finer clause blocks for evidence by ID, measured against the retrieval ceiling. Third, a reviewer screen with source-page navigation and persisted corrections. Fourth, domain validation with independent human labels, a double-labelled subset and a document-disjoint holdout. Fifth, field-bound numbers, scoring each number in its own field and cell. Sixth, adapter fine-tuning of Qwen3-VL 8B after error analysis, shown on held-out documents of the same types.

cards.title: Engineering takeaways from the evaluation
questions: what are the takeaways of the document intelligence evaluation
what did the document intelligence study teach her
what is the main lesson about method and model
why keep failures in the denominator
why report numeric recall beside text metrics
why separate provenance from correctness

what is the 43-point swing lesson
what is the masking lesson in numbers
what would she tell a team picking a local document model
what are the six engineering takeaways

tags: method is part of the model
cards.answer: Six lessons. Define the problem as extraction types, not OCR: six tasks with six metrics exposed a 43-point swing one accuracy number would have averaged away. The method is part of the model, since self-check helped 7B by 26.5 points and hurt 8B by 43.5. Keep failures in the denominator, which made the thinking-build collapse and the first Nemotron result visible. Report numbers beside text, because masking raised word F1 by 0.067 and cut numeric recall by 0.178. Separate provenance from correctness. And treat a bad score as a configuration until proven otherwise.
